evidence.why: A current axis must reach its threshold.
Input acceptance, alternatives and mutually exclusive neutral condition.

facts.rationale: Separates the accepted C-stick path from the shared selector's neutral fallback without removing supported aerial, Float or item-substitution knowledge.
facts.value: Implements the fresh C-stick command used to request and directionally select an aerial attack in common aerial handling and Peach's attack-during-Float path. When this predicate succeeds, the selector uses current C-stick coordinates to choose forward, back, up, or down aerial behavior; its neutral aerial branch requires both selected axes below threshold and therefore belongs to the fallback main-stick route, not an accepted fresh C-stick edge. Callers retain their held-item and character-specific dispatch alternatives.

evidence.why: Held-item precondition, neutral condition and directional dispatch.

facts.rationale: Corrects the claimed neutral outcome while preserving mode eligibility, item classification, directional dispatch and caller ownership.
facts.value: Qualifies a fresh directional C-stick command for held-item throwing. The dispatcher uses accepted C-stick coordinates and signed angle to choose upward, downward, forward or backward throw behavior. Its both-axes-below neutral branch is not reachable from an accepted fresh C-stick edge; that branch belongs to the shared fallback input route. C-stick acceptance requires Single-Button Mode to be off or the held item's article-defined action classification to be zero. The caller establishes held-item validity and performs state entry.

evidence.why: Exact edge and strict angle guard.
Signed atan2f with absolute X only.

facts.rationale: Replaces a misleading symmetric-horizontal description with the exact signed-angle restriction while preserving the supported recovery role.
facts.value: Recognizes a new absolute-horizontal C-stick threshold crossing for directional floor recovery, additionally requiring the signed angle atan2f(current Y, ABS(current X)) to be strictly below p_ftCommonData->x20_radians. This is a one-sided angular guard, not a symmetric sufficiently-horizontal test. The caller uses the signed current X coordinate to select a facing-relative forward or backward get-up roll; the predicate itself performs no transition.
